versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 13090 (63 FR 36151, PDF pages 1-2 of the 1998-07-02 issue; sha256 030b83d9...), headed Executive Order 13090 of June 29, 1998, President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History, matching the census register row (1998-06-29). Text and inventory: eight scopes cover sections 1 through 3(d) to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory commission. Ending: Executive Order 13225 section 3(c) revokes Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, effective September 30, 2001 (section 5). The report deadline in section 2(c) and the report-relative termination in section 3(d) are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); Executive Order 13136, whose recital shows the Commission still in existence on 1999-09-03, extended the life of the Commission. Original grade: Federal Register machine text.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 3(d) ends the Commission 60 days after its final report; no held source dates it, and Executive Order 13136 (1999-09-03) extended the Commission's life, so no own-terms end is claimed (owner ruling of 2026-10-21). (2) The March 1, 1999 report date was replaced by December 31, 2000: a deadline, not an end. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 13090 found Executive Orders 13136 and 13225 and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists two hits. Executive Order 13225 is the only revocation.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command that outlives the Commission: the information, compensation, support and Federal Advisory Committee Act provisions serve only the Commission.","savings_check":"Executive Order 13225 has no wording preserving the Commission or its work; sections 1 through 5 were read.","scope_check":"All eight clauses end by the same revocation. Section 3(c) of Executive Order 13225 revokes Executive Order 13090, as amended, as a whole with no exception."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 13225 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History: its continuance sections concern other committees and its revocation section revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the body.

versions.research_rationale: EO 13101 (signed 1998-09-14, 63 FR 49643-49651), read in full from the held FR text, directs executive agencies to prefer recycled and environmentally preferable products and to prevent waste and recycle: it defines terms (Part 2), creates a Steering Committee, a Federal Environmental Executive, a Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives (Part 3), sets acquisition-planning, affirmative-procurement, EPA-designation, paper-content and agency-goal duties with many dated and reporting provisions (Parts 4-6), and adds applicability, recycling-program, training and awards provisions (Parts 7-8) and the revocation of EO 12873 (sec. 901). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause; every timed provision is a performance, action or reporting deadline, not an end. EO 13423 (signed 2007-01-24) sec. 11(a)(i) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out as earlier ends or changes: the dossier's 'target provision not located' leads (EO 12843, 12845, 12856, 12902, 12969, 13031, 13134, 13148, 13149) are OFR 'See' cross-references in both directions and operative-text mentions; none amends, extends or revokes EO 13101 (EO 13134 sec. 7(b) borrows its definition of 'biobased product'; EO 13148 secs. 306, 307, 403(b), 503(b), 1001 and 1008 and EO 13149 refer to its sections). The by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13101 named only in EO 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423 (the other hits are page, document or U.S. Code numbers, for example 42 U.S.C. 13101-13109). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording, which does not revive EO 13101. The dossier's inventory was corrected: the issuing paragraph was added, mislabelled scopes (sec302-g-2 to -5, sec302-b-dup2, sec402-b/c/d-dup2) were renamed to the sections the text shows, the seven list items of sec. 302(a)(1) were merged into it, sec. 402(d)/403(a) and sec. 901/902 were split where a span held two sections, and page furniture and part headings were cut from the span ends. Limitations: bodies formed under the order (the Steering Committee, Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives) may have had their own charter lives, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (a claim-kit rebuild changed only the chain's generic_refs_excluded count 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts are not held.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13101 in full (secs. 101-903): sec. 901 revoked EO 12873 of October 20, 1993 on signing, 1998-09-14, a completed act on another order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13101 without any revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive the order it revoked, so EO 12873 stays revoked: an effect of EO 13101 survives it (accrued). EO 13423 also restates much of EO 13101's machinery as new duties of its own (Steering Committee sec. 4(a), Federal Environmental Executive sec. 6, biobased and recycled-content acquisition and 30 percent post-consumer paper sec. 2(d), waste prevention and recycling programs sec. 2(e)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902). The three current-law leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) cite EO 13101; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: the state is transferred_or_accrued because of the completed revocation of EO 12873 and the successor duties; the prefill gave no state. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

versions.research_rationale: EO 13148 (signed 2000-04-21, 65 FR 24595-24606), read in full from the held FR text, makes agency heads responsible for environmental management and sets goals (Part 2: environmental management systems, compliance audits, right-to-know reporting, 40 percent toxic-release and 50 percent use-reduction goals by December 31, 2006, phase-out planning for Class I ozone-depleting substances by 2010), planning and accountability duties (Part 3), management-system, audit, awards, training, compliance-assistance and assurance duties with 4- to 24-month clocks (Part 4), emergency-planning and toxic-chemical reporting and reduction provisions (Part 5), landscaping (Part 6), acquisition and procurement limits (Part 7), national-security exemptions and OMB compliance modification (Part 8), general provisions including the revocation of EO 12843, 12856, 12969, a 1994 memorandum and section 1-4 of EO 12088 (Part 9) and definitions (Part 10). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause. The dossier's undated 'fixed_term' own-terms (the 'within 12 months after environmentally benign pressure sensitive adhesives ... become commercially available' clock in sec. 702 and the exemption provisions in sec. 801) are conditional action clocks and exemption wording, not ends; December 31, 2006 target dates in secs. 204, 205 and 503(a) passed 24 days before the revocation and are lapsed performance deadlines, not ends. EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(iv) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out: the dossier's lead ACT:EO:13148>EO:13693 is spurious: EO 13693 sec. 16(d) amends EO 13327 sec. 3(b)(vi), striking the citation of EO 13148 there, and amends nothing in EO 13148 (the dossier flags the large EO 13693 context for reading before scope is decided; read, it holds no such provision); the 'target provision not located' leads (EO 13101, 13123, 13134) are EO 13148's own citations of those orders; the by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13148 named only in EO 13327 (a citation), 13423 and 13693 (the other hits are page numbers or a hash). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording. Inventory corrections: the issuing paragraph was added; heading-only fragments (secs. 305, 403, 404, 405, 406, 601, 701, 704, 902) were merged into their first subsection; the sentences the dossier cut mid-way in secs. 501(b)/(d), 501(e) and 503(b) were rejoined and the duplicate-suffixed scope of sec. 501(d) was renamed; page furniture and part headings were cut from span ends. Limitations: the Interagency Environmental Leadership Workgroup (sec. 306) and other bodies formed under the order may have had charter lives of their own, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (only chain.generic_refs_excluded 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts and Code note are not held.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13148 in full (secs. 101-1009): sec. 901 revoked EO 12843, EO 12856, the Executive Memorandum on Environmentally Beneficial Landscaping of April 26, 1994, EO 12969 and section 1-4 'Pollution Control Plan' of EO 12088 on signing, 2000-04-21: completed acts on other instruments, one of them a partial revocation of a surviving order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13148 without revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked, so those stay revoked: an effect of EO 13148 survives it (accrued); the U.S. Code note to 42 U.S.C. 4321 still prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 sec. 901. EO 13423 restates the environmental-management subject as new duties of its own (toxic and hazardous chemical and waste reduction sec. 2(e), environmental management systems sec. 3(b), compliance audits sec. 3(c), reporting sec. 3(g)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse; the statutory reporting duties the order repeats (EPCRA sec. 313, PPA sec. 6607, sec. 902(c)) rest on those statutes independently. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902(a)). The three current-law leads (42 U.S.C. 4321 note, 33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E) cite EO 13148; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 13168 (65 FR 58217, PDF pages 1-2 of the 2000-09-27 issue; sha256 4fd3fdda...), headed Executive Order 13168 of September 22, 2000, President’s Commission on Improving Economic Opportunity in Communities Dependent on Tobacco Production While Protecting Public Health, matching the census register row (2000-09-22). Text and inventory: ten scopes cover sections 1 through 6 to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory commission. Ending: Executive Order 13225 section 3(d) revokes Executive Order 13168, effective September 30, 2001 (section 5), which is earlier than the outer limit of section 6 (September 22, 2002). The report deadlines in section 4 and the report-relative termination in section 6 are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines). Original grade: Federal Register machine text.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 6 ends the Commission 30 days after its final report; no held source dates it, so no own-terms end is claimed (owner ruling of 2026-10-21). (2) The two-year outer limit, September 22, 2002, falls after the revocation. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 13168 found only Executive Order 13225 and the order's own texts; the OFR disposition-note machine search lists one hit.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command that outlives the Commission: the information, support and Federal Advisory Committee Act provisions serve only the Commission.","savings_check":"Executive Order 13225 has no wording preserving the Commission or its work; sections 1 through 5 were read.","scope_check":"All ten clauses end by the same revocation. Section 3(d) of Executive Order 13225 revokes Executive Order 13168 as a whole with no exception."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 13225 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the President's Commission on Improving Economic Opportunity in Communities Dependent on Tobacco Production While Protecting Public Health: its continuance sections concern other committees and its revocation section revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the body.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 13210 established the President's Commission to Strengthen Social Security and contains no provision other than those of a commission order (membership, mission, administration, reports, termination). Its termination clause reads "The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting
its final report." That clause is triggered by the date of a report and is not an end under owner ruling 2026-10-21-report-deadline; the report date is not held in any source in the repository, so it is disclosed here and not recorded as an end. Section 3 of EO 13316 of September 17, 2003 (68 FR 55255, published September 23, 2003)  revokes the order by number with the words "(e) Executive Order 13210, establishing the President ’s Commission to 
Strengthen Social Security;" and the first dated end held is 2003-09-30. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own text: the order's termination clause (\"The Commission shall terminate 30 days after submitting\nits final report.\") depends on the date of a final report that no held source dates; under the report-deadline ruling it is disclosed and not treated as an end. No fixed calendar sunset appears in the order. Searched held texts by the order's number: only the order's own copies and the revoking order cite it. No earlier revocation or supersession is held.","independent_command_check":"All commands in the order establish, staff, direct or report from the commission; none is an independent continuing command outside it. The revocation is express and unqualified, so no clause is carved out.","savings_check":"No savings language appears in the revoking order for EO 13210.","scope_check":"The inventory is the 17 scopes the packet derives from the Federal Register text of EO 13210; every scope belongs to the single commission order, and Section 3 of EO 13316 of September 17, 2003 (68 FR 55255, published September 23, 2003) revokes the order as a whole without exception."}

versions.research_rationale: EO 13783 (signed 2017-03-28, 82 FR 16093-16097; 'Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the policy (sec. 1), orders agency review of regulations that burden domestic energy (sec. 2: 45-day plans, 120-day draft reports, 180-day final reports), revokes EO 13653, three Presidential memoranda and two reports and orders CEQ guidance rescinded (sec. 3), orders EPA review of the Clean Power Plan and related rules (sec. 4), disbands the social-cost-of-greenhouse-gases working group and withdraws its documents (sec. 5), directs Interior on the coal leasing moratorium (sec. 6), orders EPA and Interior reviews of oil and gas rules (sec. 7) and has general provisions (sec. 8). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)), condition (sec. 2(e), 7(b)(iv), 8(b)) and until_event (sec. 7(c)); all are deadlines or conditions on performance, none is an end, and the order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. A report deadline is never an end and no clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it ('are hereby revoked') in the same sentence as EO 13766, 13778, 13792, 13795, 13868 and 13927; the sec. 7(a) exception ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') belongs to EO 13834 only. EO 13990 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out: 'target provision not located: EO:13790' (EO 13790, 82 FR 20237, sec. 4(c) only tells the new Agriculture task force to 'coordinate its efforts with other reviews ... conducted pursuant to' EO 13771, 13778 and 13783: a cross-reference, no amendment or extension) and 'EO:13817' (82 FR 60835, sec. 4(b) tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy 'in a manner consistent with, and when possible complementary to' EO 13783 and others: a cross-reference). A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532 through EO 14435; hyphenation and whitespace normalised) finds EO 13783 named only in EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement is recorded before or after the revocation. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name no order of this batch and reinstate nothing, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Dossier conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW (a DOE regulation cites the order) resolved in conflict_resolutions. Inventory: the dossier's 51 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 8(c); the unnumbered issuing words are not an operative clause. Inventory correction: the dossier labels the two reports in Sec. 3(b) 'sec3-i-dup2' and 'sec3-i-ii-dup2' and omits the lettered parent from other sub-items; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span unchanged and only rename the scopes (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or the VerDate footer from a page break; they are left as the dossier has them. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S4 prefill resolved).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13783 by number in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; the only exception in sec. 7(a) is EO 13834 and the sec. 7(a) list otherwise excepts nothing; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order or act; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13783 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 8(c) disclaims rights) and no continuing body. But parts of it are completed, self-executing acts on OTHER instruments: sec. 3(a) revokes EO 13653 and the Presidential Memoranda of June 25, 2013, November 3, 2015 and September 21, 2016; sec. 3(b) rescinds two Executive Office reports; sec. 5(b) disbands the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases and withdraws six of its technical documents. Revoking EO 13783 does not by itself restore any of them. EO 13990 reinstates only EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum (sec. 4(b)), and sec. 5(b) establishes a new Working Group without reviving the old documents; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds EO 13653 named only in EO 13677, 13683, 13693 and 13783, and no held order reinstates it or the memoranda. Those acts therefore continue independently of EO 13783. S4 prefill ('review', dossier conflict) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13783, EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435); U.S. Code and eCFR leads in the dossier. The present legal status of the memoranda and reports themselves is not searched here.

versions.research_rationale: EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end: Sec. 2(d) and 2(e) set 45-day and 120-day report deadlines, which are deadlines and never ends. No earlier revoking, superseding or partial-amending instrument: the OFR catalog search lists only EO 13990 (2 hits), the U.S. Code and eCFR searches have 0 hits, and a full-text search of the held Federal Register order texts for '13792' finds only EO 13792 and EO 13990 (EO 10304 matches only a Federal Register document number). No reinstatement candidate is recorded. Any earlier de facto completion of the Secretary's review is not a legal ending of the order and is not dated by a held source.","independent_command_check":"Sec. 2(a)-(e) are directions to the Secretary of the Interior that draw their authority from the order and ended with it; Sec. 3(a)-(c) are general provisions that fall with the order. EO 13990 retains no independent command from EO 13792 (its Sec. 7(f) and Sec. 8 direct rescission or disclaim effects; they do not preserve anything).","savings_check":"Read EO 13990 Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 and the whole of EO 13792 for saving or transitional wording: none for EO 13792. Accrued: the Secretary's 2017 review and reports (not dated by any held source) are past acts, not continuing commands.","scope_check":"EO 13990 Sec. 7(a) names EO 13792 in an unqualified list ('are hereby revoked'). The qualifying words in Sec. 7 ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') attach only to EO 13834, the 90-day suspension in 7(c) only to EO 13920. So all 18 clause records of EO 13792 ended together; no clause survived."}

versions.research_rationale: EO 13807 (signed 2017-08-15, 82 FR 40463-40469; 'Establishing Discipline and Accountability in the Environmental Review and Permitting Process for Infrastructure Projects'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the purpose and policy (secs. 1-2), definitions (sec. 3), a Cross-Agency Priority Goal and performance accountability system (sec. 4), process enhancements - 'One Federal Decision', permitting timetables, the Dashboard, EO 13766 implementation, CEQ and FPISC duties, energy corridors and an Interior reorganization strategy (sec. 5) - the revocation of EO 13690 (sec. 6) and general provisions (sec. 7). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are condition (sec. 5(b)(ii)-(iii), 5(c), 5(d), 5(f)(i), 7(b)), fixed_term (sec. 4(b)) and until_event (sec. 5(b)(iv)). The fixed_term is the '180 days of the establishment of the CAP Goal, or such longer period as determined by the Director of OMB' for OMB's accountability guidance: a deadline for performing a command, not an end. The until_event is 'until the design of a project has sufficiently advanced': a rule about when a project's timetable dates may be left blank, not an end. The order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(b) says 'Executive Order 13807 ... is hereby revoked'; whole scope, no exception (the only sec. 7 exception is EO 13834); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out as ends or amendments: 'target provision not located: EO:13766' (EO 13807 sec. 5(d) implements EO 13766 and redirects the CEQ Chairman's secs. 2-3 responsibilities; EO 13766 was revoked by EO 13990 sec. 7(a) the same day: nothing earlier); 'EO:13781' (sec. 5(h) tells OMB to fold Interior's strategy into the plan under EO 13781: a coordination cross-reference); 'EO:13817' (sec. 4(b) of EO 13817 tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy consistently with EO 13807: a cross-reference). Other actor provision ACT:EO:13807>EO:14030: EO 14030 sec. 5(e) does not revoke EO 13807 (it narrates that EO 13807 had revoked EO 13690 and reinstates EO 13690); it is attached as a later event on sec6 only. EO 13921 sec. 6(a) (2020-05-07; effective on signing, no effective-date wording) tells agencies reviewing aquaculture projects to 'use the ''One Federal Decision'' process enhancements described in section 5(b) of Executive Order 13807': an incorporation by reference of sec. 5(b), not an amendment, suspension or revocation of EO 13807, so no later event is attached (EO 13921 is also not among the dossier's evidence records, so it could not be attached); EO 14276 (2025-04-17, 90 FR 16993) says EO 13921 'remains in effect', and the use of the process for aquaculture continues under EO 13921 itself after EO 13807's revocation - see savings_residuals. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts finds EO 13807 named only in EO 13817, 13921, 13990 and 14030, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement of EO 13807 itself is recorded. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but do not name EO 13807 or reinstate it, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Inventory: the dossier's 52 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 7(c). Inventory correction: the dossier mislabels sub-items with 'dup2/dup3/dup4' suffixes and omits lettered parents, and its 25-character clause 'sec5-b' ('(b) One Federal Decision.') is too short for the claim-checker's quotation test; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span, rename the scopes and merge sec5-b into the adjacent Sec. 5(b)(i) (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or VerDate footer from a page break. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S1 prefill resolved).

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(b) revokes EO 13807 by number with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; sec. 7(b)'s second sentence only tells the OMB Director and CEQ Chair to 'consider whether to recommend that a replacement order be issued' (a direction to consider, not a transfer). Own-residual check, reading EO 13807 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 7(c) disclaims rights) and no body. Three things need a state. (1) Sec. 6 is a completed act on another instrument: it revoked EO 13690 (Federal Flood Risk Management Standard). EO 13990 did not reinstate EO 13690, so that revocation outlived EO 13807 until EO 14030 sec. 5(e) expressly reinstated EO 13690 on 2021-05-20 (attached as a later event on sec6). (2) Sec. 5(b)'s 'One Federal Decision' process is incorporated by reference in EO 13921 sec. 6(a), which EO 14276 (2025) says remains in effect; the process continues to be directed for aquaculture projects independently of EO 13807 (recorded here; not attachable as a later event because it neither amends, suspends nor revokes the clause and EO 13921 is not among the dossier's evidence records). (3) Functions it assigned or re-delegated (sec. 5(d) CEQ-to-FPISC referrals for EO 13766, sec. 5(f) GSA support and delegations, sec. 5(h) Interior strategy) lapse with the order or rest on 42 U.S.C. 4370m-4370m-12 and the agencies' own authority; EO 13990 sec. 8(a) saves only that statutory authority and moves nothing. S1 prefill ('review', transfer wording) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not transferred_or_accrued and not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13807, EO 13766, EO 13817, EO 13921, EO 13990, EO 14030 and EO 14276 in full or in the cited sections; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435). The present status of the Framework Memorandum of March 20, 2018 and of EO 13690 after the 2025 revocation of EO 14030 are outside this order's lifecycle and not searched.

versions.research_rationale: EO 13997 (signed 2021-01-21, 86 FR 7201-7203), read in full from the held official FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13997.txt, PDF pages 1-3; born-digital FR text layer). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The dossier's 23 clause spans (866-7333) cover every operative sentence from sec. 1 to sec. 5(c) without gaps (some dossier labels are shorthand: 'sec2-i' is sec. 2(b)(i), 'sec3-i' is sec. 3(c)(i), 'sec4-i' is sec. 4(c)(i), 'sec5-i' is sec. 5(a)(i)); inventory confirmed as complete. Deciding source: EO 14148 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8237, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14148.txt), sec. 2: 'The following executive actions are hereby revoked:' ... '(k) Executive Order 13997 of January 21, 2021 (Improving and Expanding Access to Care and Treatments for COVID–19).' (offsets 3467-3583). No effective-date wording (the machine 'effective' hits are words in other orders' titles), so effective on signing 2025-01-20; every clause first ends then, and whole_order_end is 2025-01-20. Earlier-end test: the order has no sunset, term or condition; its directives carry no deadlines (several say 'promptly'); no held source shows any directive performed and spent, and a one-time directive's performance would only make it functionally spent (noted per clause). D6 / later events: the dossier chain and actor provisions contain only EO 14148; the draft's later-event and whole-order-end proposals (OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 14148, January 20, 2025'; 42 U.S.C. 247d note) point to the same instrument; by-number scans of the held FR and APP texts found no amendment of EO 13997. Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR or text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. No draft conflicts; the U.S. Code and eCFR leads are ended-status notes, not current-law predicates. Machine searches pasted after review. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 14148 (held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14148.txt, 90 FR 8237, PDF pages 1-5, read in full): sec. 2 revokes the listed actions with no exception or savings wording; sec. 3(a)-(c) (offsets 13487 onward) directs agencies to end implementation and the DPC/NEC Directors to 'review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders ... listed in section 2 of this order and take necessary steps to rescind, replace, or amend such actions as appropriate', which is the opposite of a savings clause; sec. 4 (offsets 15059 onward) is the standard general provisions (no impairment of statutory authority, consistent with law, no private right). Own-residual check, reading EO 13997 in full (86 FR 7201-7203, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13997.txt offsets 866-7333): it states policy and directs planning, assistance and evaluation by HHS, DoD, VA and the COVID-19 Response Coordinator, all 'consistent with applicable law'; sec. 5(c) says it creates no right or benefit. It created no office, fund or private right of its own; agency actions taken under it rest on their own statutory authority and are not kept in force by the order. Nothing of the order outlives the revocation. Bounded search: both orders read in full in the held official FR texts; by-number scans of all 6,652 held FR order texts (hits: EO_14148 the revocation; EO_14246 and EO_9767 are FR page or document numbers) and of the held APP texts (only EO 14148); the U.S. Code hit (42 U.S.C. 247d note, release point 119-121, an ended-status note: 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, § 2(k), Jan. 20, 2025') and the eCFR search, read with their scope notes.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (3 FR 1995, fr-originals) prints the number 7951, is signed 1938-08-12 and is headed Withdrawal of Public Land for Lookout Station (Arkansas); the filing line is F.R. Doc. 38-2371, filed 1938-08-13. The order has three numbered sections: section 1 revokes Executive Order 6964 as to one 20-acre tract; section 2 temporarily withdraws and reserves that tract for a State of Arkansas forest-fire lookout tower; section 3 says section 2 continues in force until revoked by the President or by act of Congress. The dossier inventory (sec1, sec2, sec3) is complete; the recital paragraph is not a command. Ending: Public Land Order 3277 (28 FR 13306, held page extract jobs/selden-fr-acting/output/texts/FR_28_13306.txt, sha256 34b578b5269da96313b29b26654886623ce3d4c593e2ef336c126020562de3a7, bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-3277-EO-7951) is headed Revoking Executive Order No. 7951 of August 12, 1938. Paragraph 1 revokes Executive Order 7951 for the same 20 acres (T. 6 N., R. 14 W., sec. 27, W1/2 NW1/4 SW1/4); paragraph 2 restores the land to the public land laws at 10:00 a.m. on January 8, 1964; paragraph 4 states the intent to re-embrace the lands in the Executive Order 6964 withdrawal immediately upon the date of the order; the order is dated December 3, 1963 over the signature of the Assistant Secretary of the Interior (F.R. Doc. 63-12673, filed 1963-12-06). versions.research_rationale:
The complete official original was compared with its target page: EO 8179 has three numbered amendments, including all nested conditions; EO 8300 has one amendment of the first sentence of Rule VII section 2(b). The originals contain no sunset, completed assignment, or independent command outside those host-rule amendments. Probation and objection conditions govern recurring application rather than ending the entire order. EO 8707 and EO 8423 are later amendments, with before-and-after text retained. The earlier ACT commentary that EO 8707 ended EO 8179 item 2 is reconsidered under the owner's October 21 strike-and-insert ruling, which continues the amended clause.

The full text and operative pages of EO 9830 were examined. Its opening May 1, 1947 effective date governs Parts I, II and III. Part II replaces the Civil Service Rules, and Part III expressly names both target orders and their original dates without a savings qualification. Every original footprint therefore ends on May 1, 1947 under the owner's October 21 unnamed-instruments convention. This is the convention's named endpoint, not a claim that no substantive application changed earlier. The earlier War Service Regulations and 1946 temporary regulations are pinned and expressly disclosed as candidate earlier changes. The 1942 list does not include Rule XI. The 1946 effective-date qualification is preserved rather than converted to an unsupported exact date.

EO 9691 and temporary regulation 27.16(g) protect acquired rights, tenure and benefits. These are separately analyzed as saved acts and successor authority, not silently erased or treated as current authority under the revoked target orders. No independent target command or present application of the old target terms was identified in the bounded later-source, host-rule, savings and revival checks. The U.S. Code machine search reaches October 9 only; it is not the sole bridge to the October 14, 2026 cutoff. This is a producer proposal under the existing codebook and owner rulings, subject to independent whole-case review and human review of the disclosed earlier candidates.

Correction after independent review: EO8514 is a distinct earlier exception affecting item2. It permits Commission-approved probationary transfers into positions directly concerned with national defense without a six-month minimum. EO8707 does not subsume it. The authorization begins on August13,1940 under its immediate operative wording and is expressly revoked by EO9691 section9 on February4,1946. The acquired-reemployment-rights saving is retained without assuming all rights were extinguished or all other wartime limitations were removed. This member-specific exception and its end are pinned in the actual item2 later events and earlier-candidate disclosure; the May1,1947 named target endpoint remains unchanged under the owner convention.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9830 contains no savings clause for either target and replaces the Civil Service Rules while expressly revoking the targets. Completed appointments and promotions and acquired status may remain saved acts under successor authority; this does not by itself continue the revoked source. EO 9691 section 9 protects acquired reemployment rights generally. Temporary regulation 27.16(g) retains status and tenure and awards the same benefits as reinstatement under Rule IX, so it is a material incorporation/savings candidate. Those regulations are expressly transitional until revision of the Civil Service Rules. EO 9830 replaces the Rules, prescribes successor Commission standards and revokes the targets without preserving their terms. The bounded check identified no current application of an old target term. No finding is made that every individual's accrued rights ceased; such saved acts are excluded from continuing source authority under TC08. The separately preserved EO8514 national-defense transfer exception was expressly revoked by EO9691 section9. The general acquired-rights saving follows that revocation; no inference is made that it saved EO8514 or EO8179 as continuing source authority.

The earlier ACT commentary that EO 8707 ended EO 8179 item 2 is reconsidered under the owner's October 21 strike-and-insert ruling, which continues the amended clause.

The full text and operative pages of EO 9830 were examined. Its opening May 1, 1947 effective date governs Parts I, II and III. Part II replaces the Civil Service Rules, and Part III expressly names both target orders and their original dates without a savings qualification. Every original footprint therefore ends on May 1, 1947 under the owner's October 21 unnamed-instruments convention. versions.research_rationale: Executive Order 8399 (official Federal Register text, 5 FR 1607, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits (1) Social Security Board officers and employees, on the Board's recommendation and the Federal Security Administrator's approval, to hold state, territorial and municipal office in cooperative work with the Board, and (2) state, territorial and municipal officers in such work to serve under the Board. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. The order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. However, the order names the Social Security Board, which was abolished in 1946, so an earlier cessation is possible and the first end is not asserted (see gap); EO 11408's revocation is recorded as a later event. Partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (5 FR 2557, issue of 1940-07-16, fr-originals) prints the number No. 8480 and the date July 12, 1940 after the order and is headed Excluding Certain Land From the Chugach National Forest and Reserving it for Townsite Purposes (Alaska). The held text is a reading-order extract in which the order's body is interrupted by the issue's contents column, masthead and the first lines of an unrelated Department of Agriculture marketing order, and its signature block is printed after that marketing text. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory (15 clauses starting at character 3279 and running to 12012) is not the order; it takes page furniture and the marketing order for clauses. The order has two operative paragraphs: (1) the tract of about 9,300 acres lying within the described Turnagain Arm boundaries is excluded from the Chugach National Forest, under the act of June 4, 1897; (2) under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305, 307) the same tract is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry or other disposition and reserved for townsite purposes in connection with the construction and operation of railroad lines. I replaced the inventory with two exact spans of the held text: characters 3279 to 9328 (paragraph 1, which includes the page furniture that falls inside the boundary description) and 9329 to 9781 (paragraph 2). The numeral 9,300 acres closes the first span. Ending: Public Land Order 835 (17 FR 4948, held page extract jobs/selden-fr-acting/output/texts/FR_17_4948.txt, sha256 7d4ce09b9fbae911cb373617d34b55faf1822e143bce9b331be66ee80faa8077, bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-835-EO-8480) is headed Revocation of Executive Order No. 8480 of July 12, 1940 and its paragraph 1 revokes the order, with a proviso that the revocation does not return any of the lands to national forest status; it is signed by the Secretary of the Interior on May 23, 1952 (F.R. Doc. 52-5945, filed 1952-05-29). Earlier partial events: Public Land Order 571 (14 FR 1175, held page extract FR_14_1175.txt, sha256 2cff211ecf5ccd6926fe8639dbb569489f6bda025e32a7cd71927912502d0a6e; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-571-EO-8480) set two parcels aside for The Alaska Railroad and modified the order to the extent necessary; Public Land Order 686 (15 FR 7799, held page extract FR_15_7799.txt, sha256 ab0a69c8d7d98b4eea38e06b49f6d48a977c2e1fac1f14672a9b3a9f1ac8db34; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-686-EO-8480) revoked the order only as to Tract No. 1 (Portage air-navigation site). Selden leads: used the three Federal Register page leads (PLO 571, 686, 835), each read in full; used the statute lead 30 Stat. 11 only as the authority the order itself cites for paragraph 1 (the act of June 4, 1897, 30 Stat. 11, 36; the Act's text was not read for this claim); rejected the statute leads 49 Stat. 115, 49 Stat. 500, 49 Stat. 750, 50 Stat. 246 and 50 Stat. 522, which are artifacts of the neighbouring orders and Federal Register furniture on the same pages; read 38 Stat. 305 (the Alaska Railroad act, authority for paragraph 2) and found nothing ending a withdrawal before 1952. The 1994-on full-text search returned 0 hits. Without the three PLO texts neither the ending nor the counterevidence could be done; the inventory correction needed only the original. Federal Register full-text search (federalregister.gov API v1, 1994 on) for the order number, limited to documents published from January 1994 through 14 October 2026, checked 2026-11-06: 0 hits, complete; the search covers 1994 on only and absence of a hit is bounded to that query.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Held texts that cite 8480 by number: the bounded search found three, Public Land Orders 571, 686 and 835. Only 835 revokes the order in full. Public Land Order 571 modifies the order and Public Land Order 686 revokes it only as to Tract No. 1; Public Land Order 686 also says that as to Tract No. 2 it takes precedence over, but does not modify, the order as modified by Public Land Order 571, so the order was still in force in part in 1950. Public Land Order 835 revokes the order as an existing instrument in 1952, which excludes any earlier whole-order end. The order has no duration term. I read the whole authority act (38 Stat. 305 to 307, held in the packet as SUPPLEMENT:stat-38-Stat-305-EO-8480): it authorizes the President to withdraw and dispose of town-site areas along the proposed railroad lines and contains no expiry of that authority, so no statutory sunset ended the withdrawal before 1952. The first paragraph (the exclusion from the forest) was performed on issue, so its first end is the order date.","independent_command_check":"Two independent commands: the exclusion from the Chugach National Forest (a one-time act that took effect when the order issued) and the withdrawal and reservation for townsite purposes (continuing until revoked). No report, duty or recurring obligation. The exclusion's surviving consequence is preserved by the proviso in Public Land Order 835, paragraph 1, and is a consequence, not a continuing command of the order.","savings_check":"Savings searched in the order and in Public Land Orders 571, 686 and 835 as read in full. Residual effects are the national forest exclusion preserved by the proviso, the railroad reserve and the new withdrawals made by Public Land Order 835; each rests on a later instrument.","scope_check":"Public Land Order 835 names the order in its heading and in paragraph 1 and revokes it in full, for the whole tract, including paragraph 2's withdrawal and reservation; it does not name paragraph 1's exclusion separately but its proviso says the revocation does not return the lands to national forest status, so it preserves rather than ends the exclusion. For that reason the exclusion clause is ended by performance, not by the public land order. Public Land Orders 571 and 686 are partial and are recorded as later events of paragraph 2 only."}

savings_residuals.reason: Public Land Order 835 itself carries forward parts of the tract under its own commands: its proviso keeps the lands out of national forest status, so the exclusion that paragraph 1 of the order performed in 1940 survives as a consequence; it amends Public Land Order 571 so that the two Alaska Railroad parcels stay a railroad reserve and are withdrawn from appropriation; it withdraws U.S. Survey No. 2882 and reserves it for railroad town-site purposes and withdraws two further tracts for classification; and it opens the remaining released lands to settlement under stated conditions. These are independent commands of other instruments, not commands of Executive Order 8480, which is revoked in full.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 9301 (8 FR 1825, Feb. 9, 1943, 'Establishing a Minimum Wartime Work-Week of Forty-Eight Hours'): para. 1 sets the 48-hour minimum workweek 'for the duration of the war', paras. 2-4 bind agencies and contractors and give the War Manpower Commission Chairman interpretive and regulatory power, para. 5 is a non-conflict clause for hours and wage laws. It has no dated term; the 'duration of the war' wording is the only own-term. I read the complete held EO 9607 (10 FR, Aug. 31, 1945, 'Revoking Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 1943'): its one operative sentence orders that 'Executive Order 9301 of February 9, 1943, establishing a minimum wartime workweek of forty-eight hours, be, and it is hereby, revoked', with no condition, exception or savings language, so the whole order ended on signing, Aug. 30, 1945. D6 self-check: the catalog 'See: EO 9333' cross-reference is a mismatch (EO 9333 is a Civil Service Schedule A amendment; I read the held pages). The only other held order that names EO 9301 is EO 9332 (Solid Fuels Administration for War, Apr. 19, 1943), which merely says solid-fuels directives must not conflict with WMC directives issued under EO 9301 and amends nothing; it predates the revocation and cannot revive the order. Other numeric hits in the corpus (EO 10366, 10648) are Federal Register page numbers. No held later instrument revives or re-enacts the workweek rule. The 'duration of the war' term could not have ended before the Aug. 30, 1945 revocation on any reading that I can support from the held record (formal war-termination proclamations came later), so no earlier own-term ending changes the NO. Provisional NO hypothesis only.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 9301 (February 9, 1943, Franklin D. Roosevelt; 8 FR 1825, issue of Thursday, February 11, 1943), read in full in the held Federal Register text, declares that "For the duration of the war" no plant or place of employment is deemed to make the most effective use of manpower if its minimum workweek is under 48 hours (section 1, inside the lead row of the machine inventory), directs agencies to require contractors to comply (2), authorizes the Chairman of the War Manpower Commission to interpret the order and issue policies, directives and regulations and to set a different workweek in particular cases (3), requires agencies to comply (4) and states that the order is not to supersede other hours or wage laws (5). EO 9607 (August 30, 1945), held Federal Register text, revokes it by number in one sentence. The phrase "For the duration of the war" is an own-terms condition; no held instrument or source fixes a legal end of the war before August 30, 1945, and EO 9607 revokes the order outright without reciting that it had lapsed, so the first end is the express revocation.

versions.research_rationale: EO 9303 (Feb. 11, 1943; 8 FR 1911) has three operative paragraphs amending the Foreign Service Regulations of EO 7968: para. 1 rewrites item 30 of the Tariff of Foreign Service Fees (no fee for notarial and other services to foreign officials who give reciprocal courtesies); para. 2 revokes secs. V-49 to V-52; para. 3 deletes 'in the handwriting of the officer' from sec. V-54(d). The 1989 Codification gives 'Revoked by EOs 9521, 10697'. EO 9521 revoked the listed orders only as of the issuance of Secretary of State regulations superseding them, and EO 9591 (1945) and EO 9767 (1946) still describe the Tariff as amended by this order, so EO 9521 had not operated on the tariff item by 1946; EO 10697 sec. 7 revoked whatever remained, effective March 1, 1957. Every clause is terminated by 1957 at the latest, but which date ends each paragraph depends on Secretary of State regulations not held, so first_end is left open. The para. 1 table is printed with the item number misread as '80' in the OCR. No human certification is asserted.

The order's effects were fee exemptions and regulation text for consular services; services already rendered without fee are completed transactions, not continuing effects. Bounded search: this order, EO 9521, EO 9591, EO 9767 and EO 10697 in full.

versions.research_rationale: EO 9591 of July 21, 1945 (official text 10 FR 9205, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full). The OCR interleaves columns: the order's heading, enacting clause and paragraphs 1-2 run continuously, then text of EO 9592 and a Civil Service Commission rule intervene before the signature block 'July 21,1945' with F.R. Doc. 45-13508 (EO 9592 carries 45-13509 and its own signature), so the order consists of paragraphs 1 and 2 only. Paragraph 1's opening words are quoted up to the parenthetical citation because the OCR fuses footnote markers to the cited order numbers there (the fused figures are not valid order numbers); the parenthetical cites EO 7968 as amended by EOs 8297, 9303, 9407 and 9507. Paragraph 1 amends Tariff Items 6, 8 and 34; paragraph 2 amends section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations. EO 9767 (1946) and EO 10473 (1953) changed other sub-items of Item 6 but not the eighth heading 'Issue of card or certificate of identity and registration' (EO 10473 inserts a new item immediately below it, so it still stood in 1953), Item 8 or Item 34; EO 10639 (1955) deleted only Items 1-5. EO 10697 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribed a complete new Tariff effective March 1, 1957 and in section 7 revoked EO 9591, so paragraph 1's clauses first ended 1957-03-01. Paragraph 2 is left open (see the gap): its host section V-23 may have lapsed earlier. This is a partial claim: original text, clause inventory, savings and later-source search are asserted; the ending is not.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. Paragraph 2's wording change and revocation in section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations created no fund, office, property or vested right either.

versions.research_rationale: EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled "Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions."' (OCR prints the number '928.9'; the date and title identify EO 9789). EO 9818 states no effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1947-01-07. This resolves the draft's undated-ending conflict. No earlier end was found: EO 9789 has no expiry or condition, no evidence shows any directive was fully performed before supersession, and the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus and the U.S. Code/eCFR hits (historical notes) show no other event. All clauses first ended 1947-01-07, the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9818 contains no savings clause for EO 9789, but it re-establishes the same Philippine Alien Property Administration in the Office for Emergency Management with the same functions (its paragraphs 1-8 track EO 9789's, now naming the Attorney General as the Custodian's successor), so the Administration, its personnel and the property already transferred to it under EO 9789 between October 14, 1946 and January 7, 1947 carried on under EO 9818's own terms. Those transfers are accrued results; the continuing authority after January 7, 1947 is EO 9818's, not EO 9789's. Paragraph 7's amendment of EO 9142 is likewise restated in EO 9818 paragraph 7.

first_end.effective_date_basis: EO 9818 states no effective date (unlike EO 9789, which had one), so it took effect when signed, January 7, 1947 (date line 'January 7, 1947'; FR filing line 'Filed, Jan. 8, 1947'). The OCR prints the superseded order's number as '928.9'; the date October 14, 1946 and the quoted title identify EO 9789.

In implementing the policy set forth in section 
1 of this order, the head of each agency shall: 
(a) improve energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas emissions of the 
agency, through reduction of energy intensity by (i) 3 percent annually 
through the end of fiscal year 2015, or (ii) 30 percent by the end of fiscal 
year 2015, relative to the baseline of the agency’s energy use in fiscal 
year 2003; 
(b) ensure that (i) at least half of the statutorily required renewable energy 
consumed by the agency in a fiscal year comes from new renewable sources, 
and (ii) to the extent feasible, the agency implements renewable energy 
generation projects on agency property for agency use; 
(c) beginning in FY 2008, reduce water consumption intensity, relative to 
the baseline of the agency’s water consumption in fiscal year 2007, through 
life-cycle cost-effective measures by 2 percent annually through the end 
of fiscal year 2015 or 16 percent by the end of fiscal year 2015; 
(d) require in agency acquisitions of goods and services (i) use of sustainable 
environmental practices, including acquisition of biobased, environmentally 
preferable, energy-efficient, water-efficient, and recycled-content products, 
and (ii) use of paper of at least 30 percent post-consumer fiber content; 
(e) ensure that the agency (i) reduces the quantity of toxic and hazardous 
chemicals and materials acquired, used, or disposed of by the agency, (ii) 
increases diversion of solid waste as appropriate, and (iii) maintains cost- 
effective waste prevention and recycling programs in its facilities; 
(f) ensure that (i) new construction and major renovation of agency buildings 
comply with the Guiding Principles for Federal Leadership in High Perform-
ance and Sustainable Buildings set forth in the Federal Leadership in High 
Performance and Sustainable Buildings Memorandum of Understanding 
(2006), and (ii) 15 percent of the existing Federal capital asset building 
inventory of the agency as of the end of fiscal year 2015 incorporates 
the sustainable practices in the Guiding Principles; 
(g) ensure that, if the agency operates a fleet of at least 20 motor vehicles, 
the agency, relative to agency baselines for fiscal year 2005, (i) reduces 
the fleet’s total consumption of petroleum products by 2 percent annually 
through the end of fiscal year 2015, (ii) increases the total fuel consumption 
that is non-petroleum-based by 10 percent annually, and (iii) uses plug- 
in hybrid (PIH) vehicles when PIH vehicles are commercially available at

and contracts entered into after the date of this order for lessor or contractor 
operation of Government-owned buildings or vehicles facilitate the agency’s

authority, and fleet data management practices, by revising agency fleet 
management review and approval procedures to include the Chief Sustain-
ability Officers designated under this section and section 8 of this order;

and work-related travel practices for Federal employees that foster workplace 
vehicle charging, encourage telecommuting, teleconferencing, and reward 
carpooling and the use of public transportation, where consistent with agency 
authority and Federal appropriations law; 
(g) ensure regional agency actions consider and are consistent with, sustain-
ability and climate preparedness priorities of States, local governments, and 
tribal communities where agency facilities are located; 
(h) foster outstanding performance and excellence in agency efforts to 
implement this order through opportunities such as agency leadership award 
programs; 
(i) continue implementation of formal Environmental Management Systems 
(EMS) where those systems have proven effective and deploy new EMSs 
where appropriate; and 
(j) notwithstanding the limitations on implementation in section 17 of 
this order, apply, where feasible and appropriate, the strategies and plans 
to achieve the goals of this order in whole or in part with respect to 
fueling, operation, and management of tactical or emergency vehicles and 
to the activities and facilities of the agency that are not located within 
the United States.

Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 13136 of September 3, 1999
Amendment to Executive Order 13090, President’s Commis-
sion on the Celebration of Women in American History
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, and in accordance with the provisions
of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.), in
order to extend the life of the President’s Commission on the Celebration
of Women in American History (‘‘Commission’’) to provide additional time
to develop support systems and test the viability of the recommendations
included in the Commission’s report to the President, it is hereby ordered
that section 2(c) of Executive Order 13090 is amended by deleting ‘‘March
1, 1999.’’ and inserting ‘‘December 31, 2000.’’ in lieu thereof.
œ–

By virtue of the authority vested in  
me by the Constitution and statutes, in­
cluding the Trading with the Enemy Act 
of October 6, 1917, 40 Stat. 411, as  
amended, the Philippine Property Act of  
1946, 60 Stat. 418, the First War Powers  
Act, 1941, 55 Stat. 838, as amended, sec­
tion 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and  
the Civil Service Act, 22 Stat. 403, and as  
Présidait of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered, in the interest of the  
internal management of the Govern­
ment, as follows:
1, There is established in the Office  
for Emergency Management of the Exec­
utive Office of the President the Philip­
pine Alien Property Administration, at  
the head of which shall be a Philippine  
Alien Property Administrator appointed  
by the President, without regard to the  
civil service laws. The Philippine Alien  
Property Administrator shall receive  
compensation at such rate as the Presi­
dent shall approve and in addition shall  
be entitled to actual and necessary trans­
portation, housing, subsistence, and  
other expenses incidental to the per­
formance of his duties. Within the limi­
tation of such funds as may be made  
available for that purpose, and without  
regard to the civil service laws, the Phil­
ippine Alien Property Administrator may  
appoint assistants and other personnel  
and delegate to them such functions as  
he may deem necessary to carry out the  
provisions of this order. Such personnel  
of the Office of Alien Property, Depart­
ment of Justice, as are engaged in the  
exercise of the functions transferred  
hereunder, may be transferred to the  
Philippine Alien Property Administra­
tion without loss of such civil-service  
status or eligibility therefor as they may  
possess. Any employee of a department  
or agency of the Federal Government  
who possesses special qualifications or  
experience of particular use to the Phil­
ippine Alien Property Administrator  
may, upon request by the Philippine  
Alien Property Administrator, be trans­
ferred with his consent and that of the  
department or agency in which he is  
employed, without loss of such civil-  
service status or eligibility therefor as
such person may possess, to a position  
under the Philippine Alien Property Ad­
ministrator. Upon application for re­
employment made to the original em­
ploying department or agency within  
ninety days after termination of the  
service of the employee in the position  
to which he is transferred under the  
provisions of this section, and upon pres­
entation of a statement by the Philippine  
Alien Property Administrator or his au­
thorized representatives, reciting the  
date of termination of sueh service, that  
the services of such employee have been  
satisfactory and that such termination  
was not the result of delinquency or mis­
conduct on the part of the employee,  
such employee shall, if qualified to per­
form the duties of his position, be reem­
ployed in his original position or in a  
position of like seniority, status and pay,  
so long as the position the employee left,  
or one of like seniority, status, and pay  
is occupied by an employee with lower  
retention preference.
2. The Philippine Alien Property Ad­
ministrator is hereby designated to exer­
cise and perform, and there are hereby  
transferred to him, such rights, privi-  
leges, powers, authority, duties and func­
tions, with respect to property located  
within the Philippines and property  
transferred pursuant to section 3 hereof,  
as were vested in or transferred or dele­
gated to the Alien Property Custodian by  
the Trading with the Enemy Act, as  
amended, the Philippine Property Act of  
1946, Executive Order 9095 of March 11,  
1942, as amended, Executive Order 9142  
of April 21, 1942, and Executive Order  
9225 of May 16, 1946.
3. The Attorney General, or such offi­
cer or agency of the Department of Jus­
tice as he may designate, is authorized  
and directed to transfer to the Philippine  
Alien Property Administrator all prop­
erty or interests vested in or transferred  
to him which were located in the Philip­
pines at the time of such vesting or  
transfer, or the proceeds thereof, sub­
ject, however, to such expenses as the  
Attorney General is authorized to charge  
against such property or proceeds. Such  
property or proceeds shall be adminis­
tered and disposed of under the direction  
and control of the Philippine Alien Prop­
erty Administrator in accordance with  
law.

ministrator shall, except as otherwise

Federal Register
Vol. 64, No. 157
Monday, August 16, 1999
Title 3—
The President
Executive Order 13134 of August 12, 1999
Developing and Promoting Biobased Products and Bioenergy
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Advisory Com-
mittee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.), and in order to stimulate the
creation and early adoption of technologies needed to make biobased prod-
ucts and bioenergy cost-competitive in large national and international mar-
kets, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. Policy. Current biobased product and bioenergy technology has
the potential to make renewable farm and forestry resources major sources
of affordable electricity, fuel, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and other materials.
Technical advances in these areas can create an expanding array of exciting
new business and employment opportunities for farmers, foresters, ranchers,
and other businesses in rural America. These technologies can create new
markets for farm and forest waste products, new economic opportunities
for underused land, and new value-added business opportunities. They also
have the potential to reduce our Nation’s dependence on foreign oil, improve
air quality, water quality, and flood control, decrease erosion, and help
minimize net production of greenhouse gases. It is the policy of this Adminis-
tration, therefore, to develop a comprehensive national strategy, including
research, development, and private sector incentives, to stimulate the creation
and early adoption of technologies needed to make biobased products and
bioenergy cost-competitive in large national and international markets.
Sec. 2. Establishment of the Interagency Council on Biobased Products and
Bioenergy. (a) There is established the Interagency Council on Biobased
Products and Bioenergy (the ‘‘Council’’). The Council shall be composed
of the Secretaries of Agriculture, Commerce, Energy, and the Interior, the
Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, the Director of the
Office of Management and Budget, the Assistant to the President for Science
and Technology, the Director of the National Science Foundation, the Federal
Environmental Executive, and the heads of other relevant agencies as may
be determined by the Co-Chairs of the Council. Members may serve on
the Council through designees. Designees shall be senior officials who report
directly to the agency head (Assistant Secretary or equivalent).
(b) The Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Energy shall serve
as Co-Chairs of the Council.
(c) The Council shall prepare annually a strategic plan for the President
outlining overall national goals in the development and use of biobased
products and bioenergy in an environmentally sound manner and how these
goals can best be achieved through Federal programs and integrated planning.
The goals shall include promoting national economic growth with specific
attention to rural economic interests, energy security, and environmental
sustainability and protection. These strategic plans shall be compatible with
the national goal of producing safe and affordable supplies of food, feed,
and fiber in a way that is sustainable and protects the environment, and
shall include measurable objectives. Specifically, these strategic plans shall
cover the following areas:
(1) biobased products, including commercial and industrial chemicals,
pharmaceuticals, products with large carbon sequestering capacity, and
other materials; and

(2) biomass used in the production of energy (electricity; liquid, solid,
and gaseous fuels; and heat).
(d) To ensure that the United States takes full advantage of the potential
economic and environmental benefits of bioenergy, these strategic plans
shall be based on analyses of: (1) the economic impacts of expanded biomass
production and use; and (2) the impacts on national environmental objectives,
including reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Specifically, these plans shall
include:
(1) a description of priorities for research, development, demonstration,
and other investments in biobased products and bioenergy;
(2) a coordinated Federal program of research, building on the research
budgets of each participating agency; and
(3) proposals for using existing agency authorities to encourage the adop-
tion and use of biobased products and bioenergy and recommended legisla-
tion for modifying these authorities or creating new authorities if needed.
(e) The first annual strategic plan shall be submitted to the President
within 8 months from the date of this order.
(f) The Council shall coordinate its activities with actions called for in
all relevant Executive orders and shall not be in conflict with proposals
advocated by other Executive orders.
Sec. 3. Establishment of Advisory Committee on Biobased Products and
Bioenergy. (a) The Secretary of Energy shall establish an ‘‘Advisory Committee
on Biobased Products and Bioenergy’’ (‘‘Committee’’), under the Federal
Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. App.), to provide information
and advice for consideration by the Council. The Secretary of Energy shall,
in consultation with other members of the Council, appoint up to 20 members
of the advisory committee representing stakeholders including representatives
from the farm, forestry, chemical manufacturing and other businesses, energy
companies, electric utilities, environmental organizations, conservation orga-
nizations, the university research community, and other critical sectors.
The Secretary of Energy shall designate Co-Chairs from among the members
of the Committee.
(b) Among other things, the Committee shall provide the Council with
an independent assessment of:
(1) the goals established by the Federal agencies for developing and pro-
moting biobased products and bioenergy;
(2) the balance of proposed research and development activities;
(3) the effectiveness of programs designed to encourage adoption and
use of biobased products and bioenergy; and
(4) the environmental and economic consequences of biobased products
and bioenergy use.
Sec. 4. Administration of the Advisory Committee. (a) To the extent permitted
by law and subject to the availability of appropriations, the Department
of Energy shall serve as the secretariat for, and provide the financial and
administrative support to, the Committee.
(b) The heads of agencies shall, to the extent permitted by law, provide
to the Committee such information as it may reasonably require for the
purpose of carrying out its functions.
(c) The Committee Co-Chairs may, from time to time, invite experts to
submit information to the Committee and may form subcommittees or work-
ing groups within the Committee to review specific issues.
Sec. 5. Duties of the Departments of Agriculture and Energy. The Secretaries
of the Departments of Agriculture and Energy, to the extent permitted by
law and subject to the availability of appropriations, shall each establish
a working group on biobased products and biobased activities in their respec-
tive Departments. Consistent with the Federal biobased products and bio-
