Title 3— Executive Order 12843 of April 21, 1993
The President Procurement Requirements and Policies for Federal Agencies  
for Ozone-Depleting Substances
WHEREAS, the essential function of the stratospheric ozone layer is shielding  
the Earth from dangerous ultraviolet radiation; and
WHEREAS, the production and consumption of substances that cause the  
depletion of stratospheric ozone are being rapidly phased out on a worldwide  
basis with the support and encouragement of the United States; and
WHEREAS, the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone  
Layer, to which the United States is a signatory, calls for a phaseout of  
the production and consumption of these substances; and
WHEREAS, the Federal Government, as one of the principal users of these  
substances, is able through affirmative procurement practices to reduce sig­
nificantly the use of these substances and to provide leadership in their  
phaseout; and
WHEREAS, the use of alternative substances and new technologies to replace  
these ozone-depleting substances may contribute positively to the economic  
competitiveness on the world market of U.S. manufacturers of these innova­
tive safe alternatives;
NOW, THEREFORE, I, WILLIAM JEFFERSON CLINTON, by the authority  
vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United  
States of America, including the 1990 amendments to the Clean Air Act  
(“Clean Air Act Amendments”), Public Law 101-549, and in order to reduce  
the Federal Government’s procurement and use of substances that cause  
stratospheric ozone depletion, do hereby order as follows:
Section 1. F e d e r a l A g e n c ie s . Federal agencies shall, to the extent practicable:
(a) conform their procurement regulations and practices to the policies  
and requirements of Title VI of the Clean Air Act Amendments, which  
deal with stratospheric ozone protection;
(b) maximize the use of safe alternatives to ozone-depleting substances;
(c) evaluate the present and future uses of ozone-depleting substances,  
including making assessments of existing and future needs for such materials  
and evaluate their use of and plans for recycling;
(d) revise their procurement practices and implement cost-effective pro­
grams both to modify specifications and contracts that require the use of  
ozone-depleting substances and to substitute non-ozone-depleting substances  
to the extent economically practicable; and
(e) exercise leadership, develop exemplary practices, and disseminate infor­
mation on successful efforts in phasing out ozone-depleting substances.
Sec. 2. D e fin itio n s , (a) “Federal agency” means any executive department,  
military department, or independent agency within the meaning of 5 U.S.C.  
101,102, or 104(1), respectively.
(b) “Procurement” and “acquisition” are used interchangeably to refer  
to the processes through which Federal agencies purchase products and  
services.

=== PDF page 256 of 268 ===
Federal Register / VoL 58» No. 77 /  Friday, April 23, 1993 / Presidential Documents
(c) “Procurement regulations, policies and procedures" encompasses the  
complete acquisition process, including the generation of product descrip­
tions by individuals responsible for determining which substances must  
be acquired by the agency to meet its mission.
(d) “Ozone-depleting substances" means the substances controlled inter­
nationally under the Montreal Protocol and nationally under Title VI of  
the Clean Air Act Amendments. This includes both Class I and Class II  
substances as follows:
(i) "Class I substance" means any substance designated as Class I  
in the Federal Register notice of July 30,1992 (57 Fed. Reg. 33753), including  
chlorofluorocarbons, halons, carbon tetrachloride, and methyl chloroform  
and any other substance so designated by the Environmental Protection  
Agency (“EPA") by regulation at a later date; and
(ii) “Class II substance" means any substance designated as Class  
H  in the Federal Register notice of July 30, 1992 (57 Fed. Reg. 33753),  
including hydrochlorofluorocarbons and any other substances so designated  
by EPA by regulation at a later date.
(e) “Recycling" is used to encompass recovery and reclamation, as well  
as the reuse of controlled substances.
Sec. 3. P o lic y . It is the policy of the Federal Government that Federal  
agencies: (i) implement cost-effective programs to minimize the procurement  
of materials ana substances that contribute to the depletion-of stratospheric  
ozone; and (ii) give preference to the procurement of alternative chemicals,
S
roducts, and manufacturing processes that reduce overall risks to human  
ealth and the environment by lessening the depletion of ozone in the  
upper atmosphere. In implementing this policy, prior to final promulgation  
of EPA regulations on Federal procurement, Federal agencies shall begin  
conforming their procurement policies to the general requirements of Title  
VI of the Clean Air Act Amendments by:
(a) minimizing, where economically practicable, the procurement of prod­
ucts containing or manufactured with Class I substances in anticipation  
of the phaseout schedule to be promulgated by EPA for Class I substances,  
and maximizing the use of safe alternatives. In developing their procurement ,  
policies, agencies should be aware of the phaseout schedule for Class II  
substances;
(b) amending existing contracts, to the extent permitted by law and where  
practicable, to be consistent with the phaseout schedules for Class I sub­
stances. In awarding contracts, agencies should be aware of the phaseout  
schedule for Class II substances in awarding contracts;
(c) implementing policies and practices that recognize the increasingly  
limited availability of Class I substances as production levels capped by  
the Montreal Protocol decline until final phaseout. Such practices shall  
include, but are not limited to:
(i) reducing emissions and recycling ozone-depleting substances;
(ii) ceasing the purchase of nonessential products containing or manu­
factured with ozone-depleting substances; and
(iii) requiring that new contracts provide that any acquired products  
containing or manufactured with Class I or Class II substances be labeled  
in accordance with section 611 of the Clean Air Act Amendments.
Sec. 4. R e s p o n s ib ilit ie s . Not later than 6 months after the effective date  
of this Executive order, each Federal agency, where feasible, shall have  
in place practices that, where economically practicable, minimize the pro­
curement of Class I substances. Agencies also shall be aware of the phaseout  
schedule for Class II substances. Agency practices may include, but are  
not limited to:
(a) altering existing equipment and/or procedures to make use of safe  
alternatives;

=== PDF page 257 of 268 ===
Federal Register / Vol. 58, No. 77 / Friday, April 23, 1993 / Presidential Documents 21883
(b) specifying the use of safe alternatives and of goods and services,  
where available, that do not require the use of Class I substances in new  
procurements and that limit the use of Class II substances consistent with  
section 612 of the Clean Air Act Amendments; and
(c) amending existing contracts, to the extent permitted by law and where  
practicable, to require the use of safe alternatives.
Sec. 5. R e p o r tin g  R e q u ir e m e n ts . Not later than 6 months after the effective  
date of this Executive order, each Federal agency shall submit to the Office  
of Management and Budget a report regarding the implementation of this  
order. The report shall include a certification by each agency that its regula­
tions and procurement practices are being amended to comply with this  
order.
Sec. 6. E x c e p tio n s . Exceptions to compliance with this Executive order  
may be made in accordance with section 604 of the Clean Air Act Amend­
ments and with the provisions of the Montreal Protocol.
Sec. 7. E ffe c t iv e  D a te. This Executive order is effective 30 days after the  
date of issuance. Although full implementation of this order must await  
revisions to the Federal Acquisition Regulations (“FAR”), it is expected  
that Federal agencies will take all appropriate actions in the interim to  
implement those aspects of the order that are not dependent upon regulatory  
revision.
Sec. 8. F e d e r a l A c q u is itio n  R e g u la to r y  C o u n c ils . Pursuant to section 6(a)  
of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act, as amended, 41 U.S.C.  
405(a), the Defense Acquisition Regulatory Council and the Civilian Agency  
Acquisition Council shall ensure that the policies established herein are  
incorporated in the FAR within 180 days from the date this order is issued.
Sec. 9. J u d ic ia l R ev iew . This order does not create any right or benefit,  
substantive or procedural, enforceable by a non-Federal party against the  
United States, its officers or employees, or any other person.

approved by the Administrator and be regis­

Territories of the United States or in the  
District of Columbia.”

an equivalent degree from a four year stand­

wherever found it is not believed that dif­

established for pharmacists in Government

Ending: Executive Order 13225 section 3(c) revokes Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, effective September 30, 2001 (section 5). The report deadline in section 2(c) and the report-relative termination in section 3(d) are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); Executive Order 13136, whose recital shows the Commission still in existence on 1999-09-03, extended the life of the Commission. Original grade: Federal Register machine text.

EO 13101 (signed 1998-09-14, 63 FR 49643-49651), read in full from the held FR text, directs executive agencies to prefer recycled and environmentally preferable products and to prevent waste and recycle: it defines terms (Part 2), creates a Steering Committee, a Federal Environmental Executive, a Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives (Part 3), sets acquisition-planning, affirmative-procurement, EPA-designation, paper-content and agency-goal duties with many dated and reporting provisions (Parts 4-6), and adds applicability, recycling-program, training and awards provisions (Parts 7-8) and the revocation of EO 12873 (sec. 901). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause; every timed provision is a performance, action or reporting deadline, not an end. EO 13423 (signed 2007-01-24) sec. 11(a)(i) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out as earlier ends or changes: the dossier's 'target provision not located' leads (EO 12843, 12845, 12856, 12902, 12969, 13031, 13134, 13148, 13149) are OFR 'See' cross-references in both directions and operative-text mentions; none amends, extends or revokes EO 13101 (EO 13134 sec. 7(b) borrows its definition of 'biobased product'; EO 13148 secs. 306, 307, 403(b), 503(b), 1001 and 1008 and EO 13149 refer to its sections). The by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13101 named only in EO 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423 (the other hits are page, document or U.S. Code numbers, for example 42 U.S.C. 13101-13109). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording, which does not revive EO 13101. The dossier's inventory was corrected: the issuing paragraph was added, mislabelled scopes (sec302-g-2 to -5, sec302-b-dup2, sec402-b/c/d-dup2) were renamed to the sections the text shows, the seven list items of sec. 302(a)(1) were merged into it, sec. 402(d)/403(a) and sec. 901/902 were split where a span held two sections, and page furniture and part headings were cut from the span ends. Limitations: bodies formed under the order (the Steering Committee, Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives) may have had their own charter lives, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (a claim-kit rebuild changed only the chain's generic_refs_excluded count 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts are not held.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13101 in full (secs. 101-903): sec. 901 revoked EO 12873 of October 20, 1993 on signing, 1998-09-14, a completed act on another order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13101 without any revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive the order it revoked, so EO 12873 stays revoked: an effect of EO 13101 survives it (accrued). EO 13423 also restates much of EO 13101's machinery as new duties of its own (Steering Committee sec. 4(a), Federal Environmental Executive sec. 6, biobased and recycled-content acquisition and 30 percent post-consumer paper sec. 2(d), waste prevention and recycling programs sec. 2(e)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902). The three current-law leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) cite EO 13101; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: the state is transferred_or_accrued because of the completed revocation of EO 12873 and the successor duties; the prefill gave no state. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

EO 13148 (signed 2000-04-21, 65 FR 24595-24606), read in full from the held FR text, makes agency heads responsible for environmental management and sets goals (Part 2: environmental management systems, compliance audits, right-to-know reporting, 40 percent toxic-release and 50 percent use-reduction goals by December 31, 2006, phase-out planning for Class I ozone-depleting substances by 2010), planning and accountability duties (Part 3), management-system, audit, awards, training, compliance-assistance and assurance duties with 4- to 24-month clocks (Part 4), emergency-planning and toxic-chemical reporting and reduction provisions (Part 5), landscaping (Part 6), acquisition and procurement limits (Part 7), national-security exemptions and OMB compliance modification (Part 8), general provisions including the revocation of EO 12843, 12856, 12969, a 1994 memorandum and section 1-4 of EO 12088 (Part 9) and definitions (Part 10). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause. The dossier's undated 'fixed_term' own-terms (the 'within 12 months after environmentally benign pressure sensitive adhesives ... become commercially available' clock in sec. 702 and the exemption provisions in sec. 801) are conditional action clocks and exemption wording, not ends; December 31, 2006 target dates in secs. 204, 205 and 503(a) passed 24 days before the revocation and are lapsed performance deadlines, not ends. EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(iv) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out: the dossier's lead ACT:EO:13148>EO:13693 is spurious: EO 13693 sec. 16(d) amends EO 13327 sec. 3(b)(vi), striking the citation of EO 13148 there, and amends nothing in EO 13148 (the dossier flags the large EO 13693 context for reading before scope is decided; read, it holds no such provision); the 'target provision not located' leads (EO 13101, 13123, 13134) are EO 13148's own citations of those orders; the by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13148 named only in EO 13327 (a citation), 13423 and 13693 (the other hits are page numbers or a hash). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording. Inventory corrections: the issuing paragraph was added; heading-only fragments (secs. 305, 403, 404, 405, 406, 601, 701, 704, 902) were merged into their first subsection; the sentences the dossier cut mid-way in secs. 501(b)/(d), 501(e) and 503(b) were rejoined and the duplicate-suffixed scope of sec. 501(d) was renamed; page furniture and part headings were cut from span ends. Limitations: the Interagency Environmental Leadership Workgroup (sec. 306) and other bodies formed under the order may have had charter lives of their own, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (only chain.generic_refs_excluded 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts and Code note are not held.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13148 in full (secs. 101-1009): sec. 901 revoked EO 12843, EO 12856, the Executive Memorandum on Environmentally Beneficial Landscaping of April 26, 1994, EO 12969 and section 1-4 'Pollution Control Plan' of EO 12088 on signing, 2000-04-21: completed acts on other instruments, one of them a partial revocation of a surviving order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13148 without revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked, so those stay revoked: an effect of EO 13148 survives it (accrued); the U.S. Code note to 42 U.S.C. 4321 still prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 sec. 901. EO 13423 restates the environmental-management subject as new duties of its own (toxic and hazardous chemical and waste reduction sec. 2(e), environmental management systems sec. 3(b), compliance audits sec. 3(c), reporting sec. 3(g)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse; the statutory reporting duties the order repeats (EPCRA sec. 313, PPA sec. 6607, sec. 902(c)) rest on those statutes independently. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902(a)). The three current-law leads (42 U.S.C. 4321 note, 33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E) cite EO 13148; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. EO 13783 (signed 2017-03-28, 82 FR 16093-16097; 'Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the policy (sec. 1), orders agency review of regulations that burden domestic energy (sec. 2: 45-day plans, 120-day draft reports, 180-day final reports), revokes EO 13653, three Presidential memoranda and two reports and orders CEQ guidance rescinded (sec. 3), orders EPA review of the Clean Power Plan and related rules (sec. 4), disbands the social-cost-of-greenhouse-gases working group and withdraws its documents (sec. 5), directs Interior on the coal leasing moratorium (sec. 6), orders EPA and Interior reviews of oil and gas rules (sec. 7) and has general provisions (sec. 8). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)), condition (sec. 2(e), 7(b)(iv), 8(b)) and until_event (sec. 7(c)); all are deadlines or conditions on performance, none is an end, and the order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. A report deadline is never an end and no clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it ('are hereby revoked') in the same sentence as EO 13766, 13778, 13792, 13795, 13868 and 13927; the sec. 7(a) exception ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') belongs to EO 13834 only. EO 13990 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out: 'target provision not located: EO:13790' (EO 13790, 82 FR 20237, sec. 4(c) only tells the new Agriculture task force to 'coordinate its efforts with other reviews ... conducted pursuant to' EO 13771, 13778 and 13783: a cross-reference, no amendment or extension) and 'EO:13817' (82 FR 60835, sec. 4(b) tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy 'in a manner consistent with, and when possible complementary to' EO 13783 and others: a cross-reference). A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532 through EO 14435; hyphenation and whitespace normalised) finds EO 13783 named only in EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement is recorded before or after the revocation. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name no order of this batch and reinstate nothing, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Dossier conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW (a DOE regulation cites the order) resolved in conflict_resolutions. Inventory: the dossier's 51 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 8(c); the unnumbered issuing words are not an operative clause. Inventory correction: the dossier labels the two reports in Sec. 3(b) 'sec3-i-dup2' and 'sec3-i-ii-dup2' and omits the lettered parent from other sub-items; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span unchanged and only rename the scopes (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or the VerDate footer from a page break; they are left as the dossier has them. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S4 prefill resolved).

rationales.exact_text: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13783 by number in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; the only exception in sec. 7(a) is EO 13834 and the sec. 7(a) list otherwise excepts nothing; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order or act; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13783 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 8(c) disclaims rights) and no continuing body. But parts of it are completed, self-executing acts on OTHER instruments: sec. 3(a) revokes EO 13653 and the Presidential Memoranda of June 25, 2013, November 3, 2015 and September 21, 2016; sec. 3(b) rescinds two Executive Office reports; sec. 5(b) disbands the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases and withdraws six of its technical documents. Revoking EO 13783 does not by itself restore any of them. EO 13990 reinstates only EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum (sec. 4(b)), and sec. 5(b) establishes a new Working Group without reviving the old documents; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds EO 13653 named only in EO 13677, 13683, 13693 and 13783, and no held order reinstates it or the memoranda. Those acts therefore continue independently of EO 13783. S4 prefill ('review', dossier conflict) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13783, EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435); U.S. Code and eCFR leads in the dossier. The present legal status of the memoranda and reports themselves is not searched here.

EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.

shared_rationale_references.resolved_text: EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.

EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. Paragraph 2's wording change and revocation in section V-23 of the Foreign Service Regulations created no fund, office, property or vested right either.

EO 9789 of October 14, 1946 (official text 11 FR 11981, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line, F.R. Doc. 46-18658) establishes the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defines its functions in nine paragraphs; it takes effect October 14, 1946 (paragraph 9). The text is printed across columns interrupted by the issue's contents and codification guide, so paragraph 2 is inventoried in two quoted parts (before and after the interruption); no other text belongs to the order. EO 9788, signed the same day (F.R. Doc. 46-18657) and effective October 15, 1946, terminated the Office of Alien Property Custodian and moved its functions to the Attorney General; it is recorded as a later event on the clauses that direct the Custodian to act, because it changed who performed them without ending them. EO 9818 of January 7, 1947 (12 FR 133, read in full) re-issues the order with changes and in paragraph 9 provides 'This order supersedes Executive Order ... of October 14, 1946, entitled "Establishing the Philippine Alien Property Administration and defining its functions."' (OCR prints the number '928.9'; the date and title identify EO 9789). EO 9818 states no effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1947-01-07. This resolves the draft's undated-ending conflict. No earlier end was found: EO 9789 has no expiry or condition, no evidence shows any directive was fully performed before supersession, and the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus and the U.S. Code/eCFR hits (historical notes) show no other event. All clauses first ended 1947-01-07, the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text, not compared with page images.

EO 9818 contains no savings clause for EO 9789, but it re-establishes the same Philippine Alien Property Administration in the Office for Emergency Management with the same functions (its paragraphs 1-8 track EO 9789's, now naming the Attorney General as the Custodian's successor), so the Administration, its personnel and the property already transferred to it under EO 9789 between October 14, 1946 and January 7, 1947 carried on under EO 9818's own terms. Those transfers are accrued results; the continuing authority after January 7, 1947 is EO 9818's, not EO 9789's. Paragraph 7's amendment of EO 9142 is likewise restated in EO 9818 paragraph 7.
